evidence.quote: I anticipate that it will be appropriate to begin easing monetary policy later this year.
If the labor market cools too much and unemployment continues to increase and is driven by layoffs, I would see it as appropriate to cut rates sooner rather than later.
This continued rebalancing suggests that inflation will continue to move down toward our 2 percent target.
The labor market likewise has seen substantial rebalancing and nominal wage growth moderating as a result—even while keeping up with inflation.
especially as upside risks to inflation and downside risks to employment have become much more balanced.

parsed.rationale: The speech is mostly about economic measurement, but its closing outlook signals easing later this year, describes disinflation and labor-market cooling, and leans toward cutting sooner if layoffs rise. The hawkish caveat of holding rates longer is secondary, so the net signal is moderately dovish.
